ui.window.title: {app} v{ver} — Money / AI Control / Battle Injection / Spectate Capture
tip.money:
[Add money] Sets the treasury of the selected faction to the value in the box.

Useful while watching (AI campaign) so a faction does not collapse from lack of funds. Affects that faction only; it does not change game rules.
tip.goal1:
[Goal 1 - AI command in battle] Hands your army to the engine's NATIVE battle AI (not a scripted AI) so it fights on par with the enemy.

- all-ai = whole army to the AI; auto = automatic; human = back to manual; stop = end.
- This row is a direct field write: it affects only this battle's army objects, with no residue.
- The battle_ai row above is the more thorough path, but it does leave residue - see the ? next to it.
tip.goal2:
[Goal 2 - watching the campaign] Gives your faction to the campaign AI to develop on its own (faction + CAI manager writes); you just watch.

- AI-ify: the selected faction expands and takes turns by itself.
- Restore: hands control back (only factions changed in this session).
- Combine with Add money, otherwise the faction may die broke (the game continues afterwards, so you can keep watching).
tip.goal3:
[Goal 3 - watching AI civil wars] Battles between AI factions are normally AUTO-RESOLVED and you never see them; this forces them to actually load so you can watch.

- Type: siege / field / naval (siege only by default).
- PRE unit count: skip battles that are too small.
- Whitelist / blacklist: only want (or exclude) certain factions.
- Capture rate: external polling was ~17% historically (many missed); the A1 hook path awaits live acceptance.

dlg.ba_close.body:
If you quit now battle_ai stays enabled (it resets when the game process ends, but in this session it affected every battle).

Write 0 first?

Yes = switch it off, then quit
No = quit anyway
Cancel = do not quit
help.risk:
[Risks and how to undo]
battle_ai is process-wide: after enabling, loading a save or re-entering the campaign does not reset it, and every later battle goes to the AI. Only a game restart or clicking Cancel turns it off - do that BEFORE saving or quitting.
Battle injection writes army fields directly and only affects the current battle, with no such residue.
help.title: How to use
help.body:
1. Engine: pick the engine build matching your game process (6115 / 6118), then Connect.
2. Refresh factions: read the campaign faction list (must be on the campaign map).
3. AI-ify (watch): hand the selected faction to the CAI; Restore reverts only factions changed in this session.
4. Battle injection: all-ai / auto / human / stop decides who commands a battle.
5. Watch filter: only load AI battles matching your strength / army-count thresholds.
6. Log: all diagnostics appear here (the packaged build has no console).
7. Language: switch zh/en from the top-right dropdown; takes effect after restart. Hover the ? icon next to each area for a detailed explanation.
8. About: version / build time / MIT licence / repository.

Administrator rights are required: memory writes use OpenProcess / WriteProcessMemory.

about.title: About
about.tagline: Battle handover / AI spectating / AI civil-war watching
tip.columns:
[Faction list columns]
- Faction = the faction name.
- Clan / Religion = the faction's state-religion key (faction+0x6d4) translated through your language file.
WARNING: it shows whatever name YOUR language file has. Vanilla uses Buddhist/Shinto/Christian etc.; if you run a mod that renames religions (e.g. random_sengoku_camps rewrites religions.loc to East/West/Third Army), you will see those names - vanilla has no East/West Army, that is just the mod's naming. Treat this column as a hint, not as clan allegiance.
- Human = whether that faction is currently human-controlled (1 = you).
- Treasury = current treasury value.
- Whitelist/Blacklist = whether the faction is on your capture lists (double-click a row to whitelist it).
tip.dyn:
[Dynamic Decisive] Raises the 'worth watching' threshold as you see bigger battles:

- Base = the largest PRE unit total you have captured so far; floor = 80% of that base.
- Encounters with a side ratio beyond about 1:2 are skipped.
- With 'Split by type' checked, field and siege battles keep separate base/floor values.
- 'Reset base' clears and recomputes.
- Naval battles always report PRE 0/0, so control those with the type filter instead of numbers.

Use it to avoid being interrupted by skirmishes while watching, and only catch major clashes.
tip.whitelist:
[Whitelist] Only battles involving a listed faction are captured.

- Empty = capture everything (default).
- Select rows (multi-select / Ctrl / Shift) then click Mark Selected.
- Double-click a row to whitelist it quickly.
- Select all / Clear change the whole list at once.
tip.blacklist:
[Blacklist] Battles involving a listed faction are never captured.

- Empty = exclude nothing (default).
- Blacklist wins when both lists match a battle.
- Useful to skip minor factions or the remnants of dead ones.
tip.spectate:
[Start Capture / Stop]

- Start Capture: installs the interception (pending b9 write / hook) and starts watching AI-versus-AI battles; battles matching your filters are force-loaded so you can go and watch them.
- Stop: removes the interception, back to normal, no more captures.
- Requires Connect first and standing on the campaign map; it only affects AI-versus-AI battles (battles you take part in are visible anyway).
- Capture rate: external polling was about 17% historically (many missed); the newer hook path awaits live acceptance.

[The 'Auto ESC (deprecated)' box next to these buttons] In early versions the scale/faction filters could not be evaluated before writing b9, so battles had to be loaded first and then skipped with an automatic ESC; rejected after live testing on 2026-08-19 - the load has already happened, so it only wastes performance. Filtering has since moved entirely before the b9 write, so it is deprecated: leave it unticked.
tip.auto_esc:
[Auto ESC - DEPRECATED, leave it off]

What it used to do: in early versions the scale/faction filters could not be evaluated before writing b9, so the only option was to load the battle and then press ESC automatically to skip the ones you did not want.

Why it is deprecated: rejected after live testing on 2026-08-19 - the load has already happened by then, so the ESC just wastes performance (a whole load spent for nothing). Scale and faction filtering have since moved entirely before the b9 write.

Ticking it now only adds a pointless load-and-quit for every filtered-out battle, so leave it off. The switch is kept only to document that it existed.
tip.minimap:
[Reveal minimap - a direct memory write that lifts the fog]

Mechanism: writes the 'known' flag relation+0x7e0 = 1 for every entry in your faction's diplomacy table. The engine then believes you know every faction, so the minimap and diplomacy screens show them all.

This is NOT normal game progress (which unlocks through exploration, contact and agents); it directly edits memory to change what information is visible - effectively switching the fog of war off.

- A backup is written first; 'Restore known' writes it back.
- After applying, toggle the minimap tab once so the UI rebuilds.
- It only changes information visibility: no diplomacy values, no effect on AI behaviour.

If you are not comfortable with that, simply do not click it - it is independent of every other feature.
